blocks.content: The Indian Constitution has established an integrated judicial system with the Supreme Court at the top and the high courts below it.

rows: Single unified hierarchy for the entire nation
Two distinct hierarchies (Federal Courts & State Courts)
Enforces both Central and State laws across all court levels
Federal courts enforce Federal laws; State courts enforce State laws
High Courts and Subordinate Courts operate under Supreme Court oversight
State Supreme Courts are independent of Federal Courts in State law matters

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India features a single integrated judicial system, standing in contrast to federal polities like the USA that maintain a dual judicial system.
The hierarchy consists of the Supreme Court at the apex, High Courts at the state level, and Subordinate Courts (District and Lower Courts) beneath them.
This single hierarchy of courts enforces both Central laws enacted by Parliament and State laws enacted by state legislatures.
The integrated judicial framework was largely adopted from the system established under the Government of India Act of 1935.
frequently tested contrast: The US judiciary is dual (federal courts enforce federal laws, state courts enforce state laws), whereas the Indian judiciary is single and integrated (enforcing both).
The Supreme Court of India replaced the Federal Court of India created under the GoI Act 1935 and was inaugurated on January 28, 1950.
High Courts do not constitute a separate judicial system independent of the Supreme Court; they form part of the same unified structure.
